tax.text: She supported the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and said it would lower taxes for most Maine households.
tax.quote: This bill puts money back in the pockets of the American public with tax cuts beginning January 1st.

wages.text: She said the federal minimum wage should increase.
wages.quote: I believe it should be increased. In 2007, the last time the Senate voted on this issue, I supported legislation that raised the federal minimum wage to the current $7.25 an hour.

trade.text: She cosponsored legislation that would require congressional approval for new tariffs after 60 days.
trade.quote: The unilateral imposition of tariffs by the President without congressional oversight undermines Congress’ constitutional role and can have serious consequences for American workers and businesses

debt.text: She coauthored the Social Security Fairness Act, which repealed provisions that reduced benefits for many public servants.
debt.quote: The Social Security Fairness Act restores full Social Security benefits for the millions of teachers, police officers, firefighters, and other public servants

housing.text: She supported the ROAD to Housing Act, saying it would expand housing supply and cut unnecessary red tape.
housing.quote: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act will help communities expand housing supply in Maine and across the country by cutting unnecessary red tape

schools.text: She coauthored a federal program providing funding and flexibility to small, low-income rural school districts.
schools.quote: providing dedicated federal funding and flexibility to small, low-income rural school districts for technology, distance learning, and teacher training

safety.text: She backed appropriations legislation that increased funding for law enforcement and police and sheriff departments.
safety.quote: this bill is still able to provide judicious increases for law enforcement, avoiding layoffs of the people who are charged with combatting the fentanyl crisis

immigration.text: She supported a bipartisan proposal combining a path to citizenship for Dreamers with stronger border security.
immigration.quote: Our legislation underscores the broad, bipartisan commitment to creating a path to citizenship for Dreamers, who were brought to this country illegally through no decision of their own, while strengthening border security

guns.text: She introduced legislation requiring federal authorities to notify states when prohibited people fail firearm background checks.
guns.quote: By requiring the federal government to notify states promptly when someone fails a background check, this commonsense, bipartisan bill would help stop dangerous people from obtaining guns illegally

abortion.text: She introduced legislation to restore Roe and Casey protections and protect access to contraception.
abortion.quote: Our bill would restore the right to obtain an abortion by enacting in federal law Roe v. Wade and other seminal Supreme Court decisions

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: She voted for an amendment barring transgender athletes from competing in girls’ and women’s athletics.
gender.quote: My vote for Senator Tuberville’s amendment reflects my longstanding position that transgender athletes should not compete in girls’ and women’s athletics

energy.text: She says she has pursued lower greenhouse-gas emissions and clean-energy jobs while also emphasizing the burden of high energy costs.
energy.quote: I have worked to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and spur the creation of clean energy jobs – while retaining important American manufacturing jobs

voting.text: She sponsored election provisions requiring mail registrants to provide identification when voting and establishing statewide voter-registration verification.
voting.quote: Mail Registration: Voters who register by mail must provide proof of identification when voting.

tax.text: He has opposed tax cuts for wealthy households and called for taxing billionaires and corporations while funding broader health care and child care.
tax.quote: voting against the 2011 tax cuts for the wealthy (and by extension the state budget)

debt.text: He supports removing the Social Security payroll-tax cap to strengthen the program.
debt.quote: Making sure that wealthier people pay the same rate that working class people do would definitely strengthen the social security system overall.

housing.text: He supports building affordable housing and increasing Maine’s housing supply while cutting red tape.
housing.quote: Maine must dramatically increase the supply of diverse, affordable and energy-efficient housing to meet 84,000 total units by 2030.

gender.text: He opposed a ban on transgender athletes competing in girls’ and women’s sports.
gender.quote: Do you support a ban on transgender athletes in girls and women’s sports and the dismantling of other protections under the Maine Human Rights Act? No

energy.text: He supports reaching 100% clean energy by 2040 and moving renewable-energy projects through permitting quickly.
energy.quote: If we want to get to 100% clean energy by 2040 we need to get the Northern Maine wind and transmission projects built.

voting.text: He opposed requiring photo ID to vote and has called for protecting voting rights.
voting.quote: Should it be necessary to provide a photo ID in order to vote? No
